packageRules.description: First-party packages: their own group, never auto-merged. They are published from app-platform by this org and released together, so a bump to them is a platform decision — burying one in a group with a third-party patch loses that signal. Majors still separate via the rule below.

Group non-major npm updates into one PR per dependency type, mirroring the Dependabot policy this replaces. config:recommended separates majors already but does NOT group anything, so without this a handover from Dependabot trades two grouped PRs a week for one PR per dependency.
Same, for dev dependencies — kept separate so a dev-tool bump never sits in the same PR as a runtime one.

Majors are labelled and never auto-merged. Separation is already guaranteed: config:recommended sets separateMajorMinor, and the grouping rules above match only minor and patch, so a major can never land inside one of those PRs. This rule deliberately does NOT force groupName off — it would override the shared-CI grouping below, which is intended even for a major of our own actions. Why it matters: four grouped-major PRs were opened across rova and opshub in one week (NestJS 11 to 12 across nine packages plus ioredis 5 to 6; TypeScript 6 to 7 with vitest 4 to 5) and all four were closed unreviewed, because a 45-package diff containing a framework major cannot be attributed when something breaks.
Group shared CI (reusables + composite actions) into one PR
Auto-merge patch bumps of pinned GitHub Actions once checks pass

hostRules.description:
Read the org's own packages from GitHub Packages. Without this Renovate reports 'no-result' for every @quynhonsemiconductor/* dependency and silently proposes no updates for them — the five shared platform packages every product consumes. Confirmed from the Mend dashboard's Dependency Lookup Warnings.

The token is a classic PAT with read:packages ONLY, uploaded as an App Secret in the Mend Developer Portal rather than encrypted into this file: config-based encryption is no longer supported for Mend-hosted apps. The value never enters this repository, only the name does.
